notes: A prediction is only useful if it is calibrated: when we say 70%, roughly seven of every ten of those moves should happen. The curve plots what we said against what happened across 1,340 completed transfers since 2019.

We over-predict in the 30–50% band. Deals that stall in that range tend to die quietly rather than resolve, and the model still reads the noise around them as momentum. Of last window's twenty highest-rated moves, sixteen completed against nine for a naive baseline that simply follows contract length.
misses: The misses: we had Robert Davis at 88% to leave and he stayed; Anthony White at 24% two weeks before he went. Both were failures of the same kind — we weight reported fees heavily, and both stories were being briefed by agents rather than clubs.
footnote: Retrained weekly. Features: contract months remaining, minutes trend, squad-cost share, spending-limit headroom, age curve, reported-fee dispersion.
